title: Will Agent evaluation via MCP Stabilize Agent Networks? - Ari Heljakka
talk_summary: Speaker demos attaching agents to an evaluation engine via MCP so outputs get scored and explained, then revised. He argues eval stacks must be maintained and cost-managed, and recommends manual offline testing before wiring evals into agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach an agent to an evaluation engine through MCP; the engine scores task output and returns both a numeric score and an explanation so the agent can revise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: feedback in the form of numeric score, and also explanation of what went wrong comes back to the agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the MCP evaluator manually in an IDE/offline before wiring it into an autonomous agent, so humans can see how evaluators behave and fail.
Treat evaluators as a maintained library: create many, but also optimize and prune them because running evals costs money.
Encode a domain policy as an evaluator; in the demo, a hotel reservation agent stopped recommending a competitor after the policy evaluator was invoked.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it was invoking this hotel share booking policy evaluator even though we didn't even ask it specifically

takeaways.what_they_do: Let the agent pick relevant evaluators from a list in normal cases, but allow specific evaluators to be enforced when certainty is required.
Use repeated eval-and-feedback cycles so agents can improve when they do not solve a task in one shot, rather than only checking final output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we want to achieve is is a stabilization loop where the agent attempts certain task
